title: What Enterprise Teams Should Know About AI Video Platforms
summary: Explore D-ID's blog post about What Enterprise Teams Should Know About AI Video Platforms and more cutting-edge AI-driven technologies.
body_markdown:
-


###


It depends on process more than technology. Security review, contract terms, consent collection for custom avatars, LMS or intranet integration and content approval each add time. A pilot with stock avatars and approved sample content can usually start sooner than a full rollout, which moves at the pace of those reviews in your organization.


###


-


###


It depends on volume and standards. Trainers and communications staff can produce many presenter-led formats with approved templates. Someone should still own templates, quality checks, accessibility and approvals, and complex or high-visibility productions often benefit from experienced video producers.


###


-


###


Separate production savings, engagement and business or learning outcomes. Time and cost savings can justify the investment on their own, but they do not show whether a video communicated well. Compare outcomes against a baseline or control group, and include the full cost of setup, review and maintenance.


###


-


###


Often, yes. D-ID’s AI Video Generator, for example, is positioned for learning and development, marketing, sales and internal communications. The deciding questions are whether permissions, brand standards and approval workflows can work across teams with different needs.
